results.label: this tree ships the clean-rep count (src/challenge.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the parent tree IS the committed M13 release: it has the review periods and no rep count of its own
the fixture is the SAME shape in both trees: the same trades, the same recorded checklist rows, the same plan link and the same acknowledgements — written by each tree’s own journal module
the delivered tree creates exactly the parent’s schema: every table, index and trigger is byte-identical DDL, so this milestone adds NO schema object of any kind
and on that fixture every table is byte-identical, the settings the declarations live in included — the milestone stores nothing new anywhere
there is no rep/challenge table, index or trigger to find, and no DDL that declares either key: the schema search the negative claim rests on is empty
the two declarations ARE in the stored settings object in BOTH trees — the parent stores the unknown keys without a migration, which is exactly why this milestone needs none
the parent’s own second boot performs its M102 v1 backfill exactly once (one version row, one trade attributed) and a further boot changes not one byte
the parent’s own modules read the fixture the way the count needs: the acknowledgements VERIFY against the parent’s own fingerprints and the execution review records the stop decision
and the parent has NO rep count at all: no module and no key on the payload it serves — the absence this milestone closes, measured in the parent’s own code
the delivered tree reads the PARENT’s own file and counts exactly one rep: the clean, linked, acknowledged trade on the current UTC day
and every other closed trade is accounted for by its OWN criterion: one unlinked, two with a recorded breach, one never acknowledged
the newest trades are listed newest-first with their verdicts, so each reason is attributable to a trade and not to the trader

the fingerprints the PARENT’s own journal module computes over these rows are byte-identical to the delivered tree’s: an acknowledgement recorded under the released code verifies here, with nothing re-stamped
the declarations are read from the parent’s settings row as the trader’s own: start 2026-10-08, target 3
reading the count on the parent’s file changes NOTHING: every table’s digest is identical before and after the count, and identical to the parent’s own post-backfill state
the count is read-only with zero writes and no influence on a grade, cap, permission, guardrail decision or plan change
the parent’s own code still opens the file afterwards and sees exactly the six trades it left, with no row and no column this milestone added

scope: M115 migration: no schema object added, and the parent’s own file is read untouched: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
